titulo.texto: Stone Palma with Relief of Human Sacrifice

frase_gancho.texto: A stone fan where blood renews the divine cosmos.

puente_narrativo.texto: We continue with another piece from the ballgame: a stone palma that attached to the yoke and shows a human sacrifice.

guion_corto.texto: The palma looks like a stone fan, but it was an emblem of the ballgame. This one comes from central Veracruz and dates to the Late Classic, between 600 and 900 AD. Its relief shows a human sacrifice. Palmas were attached to the yoke, the U-shaped stone belt that reproduced the one worn by the players. Together they formed emblems or ritual markers of the game. The pieces found in tombs are votive versions, that is, offerings, made to commemorate the captains of the game. More than seventeen courts have been discovered at El Tajín, and that shows the importance of this ritual game.

guion_largo.texto:
A yoke, a palma, and an hacha: this is how the stone paraphernalia of the ballgame was completed. This is the palma. It comes from central Veracruz, dates to the Late Classic, and its relief shows a human sacrifice.

Palmas are fan-shaped pieces, sometimes with human heads or sacred animals. They were attached to the yoke as emblems or ritual markers of the game. The yoke is a U-shaped, or horseshoe-shaped, sculpture. It reproduces the protective belts of leather or wood that players wore at the waist to strike the solid rubber ball.

Palmas and yokes were carved from hard stones, such as basalt, diorite, andesite, or serpentine, with low reliefs and incisions. Interlaced scrolls are a very common motif.

The pieces found in tombs are votive stone versions, made to commemorate the captains of the game. That shows that the game was much more than a sport.

El Tajín, in central Veracruz, is the best example. More than seventeen courts have been discovered in that city, and for that reason it is considered a major center of the ritual ballgame.

That this palma shows a human sacrifice points to the ritual character of the game. Exactly which scene it represents has not been established.

texto: Look for the relief of the human sacrifice.
Notice the fan shape of the palma.
Imagine the palma attached to a U-shaped yoke.

texto.pregunta: Myth: Stone palmas were weapons or shields of soldiers.
texto.respuesta: Reality: They were emblems of the ballgame. They were attached to the yoke, the U-shaped stone belt, and together they formed ritual markers.
